title: Lift a prescribed top residue basis to a complete integral triangle
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and put $R_{n,T}=(R/\varpi^n)_T$ and $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R_{n,T}$, using constant sheaves and inverse limits [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Use the unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A complex $M$ is quotient-tower complete if its canonical quotient maps exhibit it as $R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T})$, with the quotient transitions and with the terms restricted to $B_T$-scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Suppose $T$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and evaluation at $T$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ be quotient-tower complete. Write $M_1=M\otimes^L_{B_T}k_T$. Fix integers $a\leq b$ and assume that $M_1$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ on every site object: for each $V\to T$ and degree-zero $k_V$-module sheaf $N$, $H^j((M_1|_V)\otimes^L_{k_V}N)=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Fix a finite integer $r\geq0$ and an isomorphism $\theta:k_T^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^b(M_1)$. No freeness or local constancy is assumed for the other cohomology sheaves. Put $P=B_T^{\oplus r}$. The canonical reduction map $H^b(M)\to H^b(M_1)$ is an epimorphism of $B_T$-module sheaves and is surjective on $T$-sections. There are $f:P[-b]\to M$ and a distinguished triangle
$$P[-b]\xrightarrow{f}M\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow P[-b+1]$$
with $L$ quotient-tower complete. The canonical derived reduction of $P[-b]$ is $k_T^{\oplus r}[-b]$, via the coefficient quotient on its standard generators; writing $f_1$ for the reduction through this identification, one has $H^b(f_1)=\theta$. For $r=0$, $P=0$ and $f$ is the unique morphism from zero. These assertions hold also for $a=b$ and $T=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Use strict DVR reduction triangles to propagate the residue bounds to all positive quotient levels and to prove that their top cohomology transitions are epic. Compare the chosen complete tower with this flat K-flat tower through a common K-flat roof; the uniquely specified tensor transitions agree. The bounded epimorphic derived-limit theorem gives the same bounds for M, in particular H^(b+1)(M)=0.

proof.text: The normalized ordinary extension of the coefficient unit is the residue unit. Preservation of finite products extends this identification to the rank-r free module, including r=0. Apply the existing K-flat counit comparison for the free single complex. Naturality of the exact restriction localization comparison and the single-complex comparison identify the derived unit with precisely freeCellQuotient, not an unspecified scalar multiple.

proof.text: The finite free source P is projective and the product coefficient quotient q is epic. Lift q followed by the restriction of theta through topReduction. The projective single-complex/homology bijection realizes that lift by f:P[-b]→M. Naturality of the derived unit and compatibility of restriction with single homology identify its reduced top homology. Cancel q and use faithfulness of restriction to obtain exactly theta.

proof.text: Complete f to a distinguished triangle. The free source is quotient-tower complete by the completed free-resolution theorem. Use the unit-compatible Roos/intrinsic completeness equivalence to translate both complete vertices into vanishing of the local principal-localization internal-Hom tests. Exact slice restriction and covariant internal Hom take the triangle to a distinguished triangle, so the third local test vanishes. Translate back to quotient-tower completeness of the cone.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q97-c73cbbce2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and all of its proof in full: 8 steps, no new nodes, statement unchanged except the quasi-compact citation. Checked the statement of every cited node and Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09C3 (lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex: lift a completed free module onto H^b, then take the cone). Steps 1-5, 7 and 8 are correct. Step 1: det-prop-sfb (3) and the regular-quotients node give the exact sequence 0→B_T→B_T→k_T→0 for any T. Step 2: the residue-bounds lemma gives H^{b+1}(M)=0 with matching hypotheses. Step 3: a flat-term K-flat representative, the normalized regular-quotient sequence, the SES triangle and the long exact sequence give that H^b(M)→H^b(M_1) is an epimorphism. Step 4: exact terminal evaluation gives cycle lifts and the chain map from P[-b]. Step 5: P[-b] is K-flat, the standard-generator reduction holds and H^b(f_1)=θ. Step 7: the constant-completion comparison with A=O_E, I=(ϖ), Â=B_T, plus closure of ringed completeness under triangles, gives that L is complete. Step 8: edge cases r=0, a=b and T=∅ are covered. Fault C4/E5 in Step 6: det-pe-milnor-epimorphic computes the derived limit as Cone(1-T)[-1] with the ordinary sheaf product. The step then switches to the strict-tower R lim functor. No cited statement identifies that cone with the Roos derived limit in D(B_T) that quotient-tower completeness requires; this needs exact pro-étale products, which the step uses without citing. Repaired by citing the same-unit node lem-sf-completed-coefficient-free-resolution (reviewed pass). It states verbatim that every B_T^{⊕r} placed in a single degree is quotient-tower complete through its actual projections, and it was the old parent's citation. No cycle. Updated proof_deps and dropped the det-pe-milnor-epimorphic and strict-tower-homotopy-limit tool_uses. The remaining tool_uses are generic tools and are accepted.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
